Hi Jared 1 thanks for the list, and great questions. Attached are two artifacts: acme-latency-report-20260524.pdf (summary) and acme-benchmarks-20260524.csv (detailed runs). Highlights below (short version):

Test config (representative):
- Model: redwood/touv2-13B (Q4F16 quantized)
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 80GB (single GPU runs); test harness used our continuous-batching driver
- Batch sizes: 1 (pure low-latency), 8, 16 (for throughput profiles)
- Sequence lengths: 512, 2048, 8192 tokens (we included long-context runs per your ask)

Key numbers (single A100, warm KV cache):
- 512 tokens: p50 48ms, p95 112ms, p99 180ms | throughput ~3,600 tokens/s
- 2048 tokens: p50 210ms, p95 420ms, p99 680ms | throughput ~2,300 tokens/s
- 8192 tokens: p50 880ms, p95 1,450ms, p99 2,100ms | throughput ~900 tokens/s

Cold cache delta: expect ~1525% higher p95 on first request depending on prompt prefix size (we measure cold vs warm in the CSV).

Concurrency guidance: with our inference router, a single A100 can sustain ~10 concurrent low-latency sessions at sequence length ~512 with 12ms scheduling overhead (see column "effective_sessions" in CSV). For higher concurrency, we recommend horizontal scaling + prefix caching.

Notes: these runs used q4f16 quantization; if you need float16 full-precision runs we can provide those too (higher latency but better quality in tail cases). Also happy to run a short smoke test against a sample prompt set you provide.

Attachments: acme-latency-report-20260524.pdf; acme-benchmarks-20260524.csv

If helpful I can hop on a 20m call to walk through the CSV and recommendations.


Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
